title: Testing admissibility as an alignment constraint on a small decision agent

original_idea.body: Testing admissibility alignment (arXiv:2601.01816) in a toy gridworld/text task; measure harm prevented vs missed by an admissibility filter on an open LLM agent.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Grounding a formal alignment criterion is useful but the chain to catastrophic risk has a skipped step.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Toy gridworld/text task + LLM agent + admissibility filter; guided execution feasible.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused harm-prevented-vs-missed breakdown; building the environment adds a workstream.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Formal-criterion grounding, open models only, independent-friendly.

novelty.reasoning: Recent criterion; empirical reach test is a plausibly-open angle.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Criterion exists; empirical grounding may be open.
